title: Haldi function jewellery: what to wear and what to skip
description: What jewellery to wear to your haldi and what to leave at home: floral and fabric pieces, why turmeric is hard on plating, and how to clean up afterwards.
keywords: what to wear for haldi ceremony
intro: Wear jewellery you would not mind getting yellow: floral sets, fabric or gota-patti pieces, and inexpensive earrings. Skip your good Kundan, AD and silver pieces, plus anything on your hands and arms. Turmeric paste is oily, deeply staining and gets everywhere, so the haldi is the one function where less precious is genuinely better.

sections.heading: Why haldi is tough on jewellery
paragraphs: Haldi paste is usually a mix of turmeric with things like gram flour, curd, rose water, milk or oil, depending on the family. That mixture is applied by many hands, often enthusiastically, to your face, arms, feet and sometimes hair. Then come the playful moments when cousins smear it on everyone nearby.

Turmeric stains are hard to remove from porous or textured surfaces. Plated jewellery can get yellow paste trapped in its grooves and around stones, and the oils in the mixture can dull the finish. Kundan settings are especially vulnerable because moisture and paste can seep around the edges of the stones. Even sterling silver, which is sturdier, can pick up stains in its crevices. None of this is worth risking a piece you plan to wear again at the wedding.

sections.heading: What to wear
paragraphs: Pick pieces that are cheerful, light and easy to replace or wash.
Fresh flowers wilt in heat, so if your haldi is outdoors in the afternoon, ask for the floral set to be delivered an hour or two before, kept cool, and fitted at the last minute.
list: Floral jewellery: fresh marigold, mogra or rose sets, or artificial flower versions. A flower tikka, earrings and a short necklace look lovely in haldi photos.
Gota-patti or fabric jewellery: light, bright and made for exactly this kind of function.
Simple, inexpensive earrings such as small Meenakari jhumkas or studs you would not mourn if stained.
A hair accessory, flower gajra or simple juda pin if your hair is tied up.
Thread or flower bracelets if you want something on your wrists, since they can be thrown away afterwards.

sections.heading: What to skip
paragraphs: Leave these in their boxes until the next function:
list: Your bridal Kundan or American Diamond sets.
Rings, bangles, kadas and haathphool, which sit right where the paste is applied.
Anything sentimental or borrowed from family.
Long necklaces that hang into the paste on your chest and arms.
Heavy earrings that you will be tempted to touch with yellow fingers.

sections.heading: If you want to wear something a little nicer
paragraphs: Some brides prefer to wear a pair of proper earrings for the photos before the paste goes on, then remove them. That is a sensible approach. Take your posed portraits first, with clean face and hair, then hand the earrings to someone you trust and let the haldi begin. Ask that person to keep a zip pouch ready so the earrings go straight into it.

Simple Kundan or Meenakari earrings in yellow, orange or green look especially good with haldi outfits for those early photos. If you are choosing a pair just for this, our [Kundan and Meenakari earrings](/women/earrings) are a light-hearted option that will not break the budget. For floral or fabric sets, a lower budget is fine; browse [pieces under ₹999](/shop?max=999) if you want something simple to pair with flowers.

sections.heading: Guests and family at the haldi
paragraphs: Everything above applies to the bride's sisters, cousins and friends too. Anyone close enough to be applying paste, or likely to have it applied to them, should keep good jewellery off. A pair of earrings and maybe a flower tikka is plenty. The function is about colour and laughter, not sparkle.

sections.heading: Cleaning up afterwards
paragraphs: If a piece does get paste on it, act quickly. The longer turmeric sits, the more stubborn the stain becomes.

For plated, Kundan or imitation jewellery, gently wipe off the paste with a soft, dry cloth. If needed, use a cloth that is barely damp, then dry the piece immediately and fully. Do not soak, scrub or use detergents, because water and friction can lift plating and loosen Kundan stones. Let it air dry completely before putting it away in a sealed pouch.

For plain 925 sterling silver, you can wash it in lukewarm water with a drop of mild soap, use a soft brush in the grooves, then rinse and dry thoroughly. A silver polishing cloth helps restore the shine. If your silver piece is gold-plated or has stones set in it, treat it more gently, like plated jewellery, and avoid harsh polishing.
Fresh floral jewellery can simply be discarded after the function. Fabric pieces may be spot-cleaned, but expect some yellow to stay; most people treat them as one-time wear.

faq.q: Can I wear my bridal jewellery at the haldi?
faq.a: It is best not to. Turmeric paste stains and its oils can dull plating and seep into Kundan settings.

faq.q: What jewellery is best for a haldi function?
faq.a: Floral, gota-patti or fabric jewellery, plus simple inexpensive earrings, are the most practical choices.

faq.q: How do I remove turmeric from plated jewellery?
faq.a: Wipe gently with a soft dry cloth, or a barely damp one, then dry it fully. Do not soak or scrub plated pieces.

faq.q: Should I take off my rings for haldi?
faq.a: Yes. Rings and bangles sit right where the paste goes and are hard to clean afterwards.
